# Python-semantics traps in Rust ports

Every one of these produced a confirmed parity defect during the v14 P2 ports (found by codex finder passes with reproduced counterexamples). Check each when porting or reviewing.

1. **str whitespace sets differ.** Python `str.strip()`/`split()`/`isspace()` treat `\x1c`–`\x1f` (FS/GS/RS/US), `\x85`, and more as whitespace; Rust `trim()`/`split_whitespace()` (Unicode White_Space) do not. Bit activity twice and buckets once. Use core `pystr.rs` — never raw `trim()`/`split_whitespace()` where Python parity matters. (`str.splitlines()` has its own, larger boundary set — render mirrors it.)
2. **Duplicate JSON object keys.** Python `json.loads`/orjson keep the LAST occurrence (by decoded key); sonic-rs preserves duplicates and field lookup returns the FIRST. Bit ids, activity, all three smallmods ports, render, and toolcall (latent). FIXED AT THE ROOT: parse.rs normalizes persisted payload Values to last-wins at parse time (json.loads parity) — landed via the queryfacts lane. `value.field_last` remains for pre-normalization or constructed values; ids keeps its internal dedup for constructed inputs.
3. **Float formatting: THREE distinct layouts.** (a) Rust `format!("{:e}")`/`{}`/plain Ryū are NOT tie-exact vs Python/ES shortest digits (counterexample: 698957826421429.2) — use `ryu-js` for digits. (b) ES `Number::toString` layout ≠ Python `str(float)` layout even with identical digits: ES gives `1e-7`, Python gives `1e-07` (two-digit zero-padded exponent; sci thresholds exp<-4 or ≥16) — canonical_json needs ES (ryu-js verbatim), render/repr-mirroring needs the PYTHON layout over ryu-js digits. (c) Python `round()` is half-even. Fuzz any new formatting path against Python.
4. **Value preservation over type-filtering.** Python stores whatever the JSON carried (`replace_all=1` stays `1`; `content: 7` becomes `str(7)`="7" where Python str()-coerces — mirror the exact Python op). Bit toolcall and notifications. Also: orjson parses `-0` (int) to `0`.
5. **Materialization drops.** The Python parse path drops events whose timestamps can't materialize. Rust paths consuming `parse_bytes` directly must apply the same drops. Bit activity_lift. (P3 moves the guard to parse time.)
6. **Code-point vs byte string ops.** Python slicing/truncation is code-point-based.
7. **Big integers.** Python ints are arbitrary precision AND Python's `/` is true division on ints (exact); Rust f64-cast-then-divide loses ulps (bit cost). Mirror Python's division order; project big ints via int-from-string (digest doc 35f43592).
8. **Regex engine dialect ≠ pattern bytes.** Byte-identical patterns match differently: `\s` (Python includes \x1c-\x1f), `\w`/`\b` (combining marks, İ). Bit buckets. See rust-regex-dialect-parity doc (d458ca8); expand divergent classes explicitly and pin the divergent inputs.
9. **Timestamp precision.** Python datetime is MICROSECOND precision; chrono keeps nanoseconds, changing near-tie sort order (bit buckets). Truncate to µs at the shared timestamp-parse owner (core parse.rs).
10. **Lenient shape fallbacks.** Python `.get()` chains fall back silently (null flat field ignored; `{}` falls back; floats priced); Rust `require_*` helpers reject. Mirror the exact Python access pattern per field (bit cost).
11. **`interrupted` is marker OR interruptedMessageId** (parser.py:405) — core's marker-only predicate was a latent divergence; unified via the queryfacts lane. When porting a predicate, diff it against the *materializer's* semantics (py/event.rs), not just the core method that happens to share its name.
